title: Assessment of Nutritional Status of Infants Living in Arsenic-Contaminated Areas in Bangladesh and Its Association with Arsenic Exposure.
ehr_evidence: Interviewers collected information by face to face interview using a structured questionnaire on socio-demographics, drinking, bathing, washing, use of cooking water and history of water use. Trained field workers took anthropometric measurements. Drinking water samples from the selected tube wells were transferred and analyzed.
summary: Longitudinal prospective cohort study assessing the association between household arsenic exposure in drinking water and infant nutritional status (stunting, wasting, underweight) from birth to 9 months in rural Bangladesh.
key_findings: Stunting rates were 10% at 3 months and 44% at 6 and 9 months.
Wasting rates were 23.3% at 3 months and 0% at 6 and 9 months.
Underweight rates were 25% at 3 months and 10% at 6 months, with 0% at 9 months.
Significant association found between stunting at 9 months and household drinking water arsenic exposure ≥50 μg/L (p = 0.009).
No significant association was found between household arsenic exposure and other nutritional indices (wasting, underweight) over time.
captured_features: Household tube well water arsenic concentration
population: 120 mother-infant pairs in rural Bangladesh, followed from birth to 9 months of age
exposure_domain: arsenic exposure via household drinking water (tube well concentration <50 μg/L vs ≥50 μg/L)
limitations: Potential change in household drinking water sources during the study leading to exposure misclassification
Lack of maternal anthropometric and nutritional intake data
Possible statistical anomaly for the observed stunting association
